swans.name: 1970s stagflation replay
swans.anchor: BLS CPI-U: +13.3% in the 12 months to Dec 1979, +13.5% for calendar 1980.
swans.effect: Prop 13's 2% cap makes the property tax a shrinking real cost, but every operating line and the discount rate rise. Holding wins on tax, loses on cost.

swans.name: 2006-2011 housing bust replay
swans.anchor: FHFA purchase-only national index fell about 21% from the 2007 peak to Feb 2011.
swans.effect: A forced sale at the wrong moment is the largest single risk in the sell path; a long hold can wait out the trough, a sale cannot.

swans.name: 2022-style inflation shock
swans.anchor: BLS CPI-U: +8.0% for calendar 2022 while the FHFA index gained only 2.7%.
swans.effect: Real house prices fall. Rent rises faster than the AB 1482 cap allows the landlord to capture if the tenancy is protected and the cap is binding.

swans.name: High-rate, low-growth decade
swans.anchor: 10-year Treasury par yield 5.10% on 12 Nov 2026 (US Treasury).
swans.effect: A high risk-free rate raises the bar every illiquid asset must clear and compresses house prices through cap-rate repricing.

swans.name: Insurance-market contraction
swans.anchor: CDI 2025: homeowners' premium $2,340/policy, plus $1,440 earthquake; dwelling fire $1,702. The FAIR Plan writes 24% of dwelling-fire policies.
swans.effect: The owner's $1,500 assumption is already below the statewide average, so a shock lands on an under-budgeted line.

swans.name: Prop 19 exclusion lost
swans.anchor: RTC 63.2(a)(1)(B): the exclusion is removed when the transferee is no longer eligible for the homeowners' or disabled veterans' exemption.
swans.effect: Moving out, or renting A long-term, forfeits the exclusion and restores the full factored base year value. This is the most expensive mistake available.
